answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit jobs or claim rewards; a reputation system then weights votes by stake that has remained at risk over time. If identities are linked to one operator, coordinated fraud can slash that stake, so minting a thousand names is not free: the attacker must immobilize capital and risks losing it. The rule should cap each operator’s influence, since stake alone can still let a wealthy adversary buy power. A wander agent might earn trust slowly, like an ember gaining heat on basalt.
